title: Typing useRef
description: Learn how to type useRef for DOM access and mutable values.

data.text: useRef has two use cases: accessing DOM elements and storing mutable values. Each requires different typing.

data.title: DOM Ref
Mutable Ref
Null Initial Value
data.text: DOM refs are initialized with null because the element doesn't exist yet. Use optional chaining (ref.current?.method()) to safely access.

terms.definition: A ref that holds a value that persists across renders
A ref pointing to a specific DOM element
Property on the ref object holding the current value

data.title: Exercise: Type a Scroll Ref
data.description: Create a component that scrolls to a section using a typed ref.
steps: Create a ref for a div element
Add a button that calls scrollIntoView on the ref
data.expectedOutcome: A component with a properly typed DOM ref and safe scroll behavior.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use optional chaining for null safety
data.takeaway: useRef typing depends on whether it's for DOM or mutable values.
